questions.title: Car on a straight road — scalars, distance & acceleration

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Amplitude: scalar
Force: vector
Momentum: vector
Power: scalar

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: The distance travelled is represented by the area under the graph line between t = 0 and t = 40 s.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
Maximum acceleration = maximum gradient of the v–t graph (the 35–40 s section):
a = (0 − 12)/5 = −2.4 m s⁻²
Magnitude = 2.4 m s⁻² (the other sections give 12/10 = 1.2 and 10/40 = 0.25 m s⁻²)

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer:
At t = 40 s the car is momentarily at rest; it then moves with acceleration −0.25 m s⁻² over displacement −150 m back to P:
v² = u² + 2as = 0 + 2×(−0.25)×(−150) = 75
v = √75 = 8.7 m s⁻¹

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.answer: Sketch a displacement–time graph from t = 0 to t = 80 s that: starts at the origin and rises with increasing gradient up to t = 10 s, continues with a constant (straight) positive gradient between t = 10 s and t = 35 s, then a decreasing gradient between t = 35 s and t = 40 s, reaching its maximum displacement at t = 40 s; from t = 40 s to t = 80 s the displacement decreases without crossing the t-axis, ending at (or up to 5 mm before) the t-axis at t = 80 s. No step changes in displacement.

questions.title: Block on a plank with ropes — equilibrium & Hooke's law

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The resultant force on the object is zero and the resultant torque (moment) about any point is zero.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
Each rope has vertical component T cosθ; two ropes act on the plank and two on the block.
Forces on the plank: 2T cosθ = R + WP
Forces on the block: 2T cosθ + R = WB
Equating the two expressions for 2T cosθ:
R + WP = WB − R ✓

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: Hooke's law

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: Elastic deformation: when the tension (force) is removed, the rope returns to its original length — the deformation is reversible and the extension falls back to zero.

questions.title: Two-source interference on a lake — wave speed & energy

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: A progressive wave is a wave that transfers energy from one point to another in the direction of propagation.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
The waves arrive at P in phase (constructive interference), so the path difference equals one wavelength:
λ = 3.9 − 2.4 = 1.5 m
v = fλ = 3.0 × 1.5 = 4.5 m s⁻¹

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer:
ΔE = mgΔh, where Δh = 2 × amplitude = 2 × 0.15 = 0.30 m
ΔE = 0.44 × 9.81 × 0.30 = 1.3 J

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: At f = 4.0 Hz the wavelength is λ = v/f = 4.5/4.0 ≈ 1.1 m, so the path difference at P (1.5 m) is no longer a whole number of wavelengths — the waves arriving at P are not in phase and no longer give constructive interference. The amplitude of the oscillation of the ball decreases.

questions.title: Electric train on a slope — kinetic energy, power & efficiency

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Power is the rate of doing work — the work done (energy transferred) per unit time.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
Useful output energy = gain in gravitational PE + work done against resistive force F:
W = (1.1 × 10⁵ × 52) − (13.0 × 10⁶ − 7.4 × 10⁶) = 5.72 × 10⁶ − 5.6 × 10⁶ = 1.2 × 10⁵ J
F = W/(vt) = 1.2 × 10⁵ / (4.2 × 52) = 550 N
(Alternatively P = Fv: F = [1.1 × 10⁵ − (13.0 − 7.4) × 10⁶/52] / 4.2 = 2.3 × 10³/4.2 = 550 N)

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
Input power = IV = 95 × 1400 = 1.33 × 10⁵ W
efficiency = useful output power / input power × 100
= (1.1 × 10⁵ / 1.33 × 10⁵) × 100 = 83%

questions.title: Resistors in parallel with an LDR — current, drift speed & resistance

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
The p.d. across each parallel resistor is the same (V), and the currents add:
IT = I1 + I2 + I3
V/RT = V/R1 + V/R2 + V/R3
Dividing by V:
1/RT = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3 ✓

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
Combined resistance: 1/RT = 1/2.8 + 1/2.8 → RT = 1.4 Ω
I = V/RT = 12/1.4 = 8.6 A

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
Current in each identical wire = 8.6/2 = 4.3 A
I = Anvq → v = I/(Anq)
v = 4.3 / (6.1 × 10⁻⁶ × 8.5 × 10²⁸ × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹)
= 4.3 / 8.30 × 10⁴ = 5.2 × 10⁻⁵ m s⁻¹

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: Light-dependent resistor (LDR)

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer:
Current through X: IX = 5.0 − 12/2.8 = 5.0 − 4.3 = 0.71 A
Resistance of the top branch: R = V/I = 12/0.71 = 16.8 Ω
R(X) = 16.8 − 2.8 = 14 Ω

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer: The battery current has decreased, so the total circuit resistance has increased; since the resistance wires are unchanged, the resistance of X has increased. For an LDR, resistance increases as light intensity decreases, so the environment of X changed such that the light intensity incident on it decreased (it became darker).

questions.title: α-particle scattering and gold nucleus — momentum & quarks

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Most of the α-particles passed straight through the gold foil with little or no deviation.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
Mass of α-particle = 4u = 4 × 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg
p = mv = 4 × 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ × 5.60 × 10⁶
= 3.72 × 10⁻²⁰ kg m s⁻¹ ✓

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
Conservation of momentum (gold nucleus initially at rest):
4u × 5.60 × 10⁶ = 197u × v − 4u × 5.38 × 10⁶
197 × 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ × v = 3.72 × 10⁻²⁰ + 3.57 × 10⁻²⁰ = 7.29 × 10⁻²⁰
v = 7.29 × 10⁻²⁰ / 3.27 × 10⁻²⁵ = 2.2 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
Change in velocity Δv = 5.60 × 10⁶ + 5.38 × 10⁶ = 10.98 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ (directions are opposite)
Absolute uncertainty in Δv = 5 × 10⁴ + 5 × 10⁴ = 1 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹
Percentage uncertainty = (1 × 10⁵ / 10.98 × 10⁶) × 100 = 0.9%

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer:
²₁H has 1 proton and 1 neutron. Each proton contains 2 up quarks and each neutron contains 1 up quark:
Total up quarks = 2 + 1 = 3

parts.label: (d)
parts.answer: A meson is composed of one quark and one antiquark.
